## Summary

Fixes #2175: a full sweep of the CI/CD annotations on the failing default-branch run [`32589574378`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/32589574378) and its green predecessors. Every error and every warning those runs emitted is now gone, and the two false negatives that let a broken release look healthy are closed.

The complete investigation — evidence, timeline, root cause per defect, template comparison and verification map — is committed alongside the fix in [`dev/log/issues/2175/pulls/2176/ANALYSIS.md`](dev/log/issues/2175/pulls/2176/ANALYSIS.md), with the raw logs and API captures beside it.

## What was wrong, and why

### 1. Error — the release job could not succeed at all (GH013)

At 17:34 UTC a `pull_request` rule with an **empty bypass list** was added to the Main ruleset. From that moment `GITHUB_TOKEN` may not push to `main`, so the 18:11 release run was rejected:

```
remote: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/main.
remote: - Changes must be made through a pull request.
 ! [remote rejected]   main -> main (push declined due to repository rule violations)
```

`2.13.5` was committed in the runner and never published. This is **not** a lost race, so the existing rebase-and-retry recovery (issue #2082) could never fix it.

**Fix.** `scripts/release-pull-request.lib.mjs` classifies the rejection and lands the same version commit through a pull request: push to a run-scoped branch, `gh pr create`, `gh pr merge --merge` (retried while GitHub computes mergeability), then fast-forward the local checkout so npm publish, the GitHub release, Docker and Helm all run against the merged tree. `isNonFastForward` now explicitly returns `false` for a rule violation so it can never be retried as a race. The branch is never force-pushed and never deleted (`no-destruction-possible` targets `~ALL`) and the merge method is `merge` (`allowed_merge_methods: ["merge"]`). The bot e-mail was also corrected to `41898282+github-actions[bot]@…` — without the numeric prefix the commit is unattributed and `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes` would block the merge on a human approval.

### 2. False negative — changesets were the release oracle

The release steps were gated on "does `.changeset` contain any `*.md`?", which cannot distinguish *nothing to do* from *a version bump landed but was never published* — the exact state an interrupted release leaves behind, and one with no failing check anywhere.

**Fix.** `scripts/check-release-needed.mjs` asks the **npm registry**, the source of truth for "is this released?". No changesets + version missing from npm ⇒ `should_release=true`, `skip_bump=true`, publish what is already committed. This mirrors the template's own `check-release-needed.mjs`.

### 3. Warning — Node 20 deprecation

`softprops/action-gh-release@v2` is pinned to the deprecated Node 20 runtime. Replaced by `scripts/upload-release-assets.sh` using `gh release upload`; the template has no reference to that action either.

### 4. Warnings — eight files in the 1350-line band

Each was reduced by extracting a cohesive module with injected dependencies (the issue #2150 §6 pattern), re-exporting every moved symbol so importers and tests are unaffected:

| File | Before | After | Extracted module |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `src/hive.mjs` | 1465 | 1323 | `hive.repository-fallback.lib.mjs`, `hive.startup-checks.lib.mjs` |
| `src/session-monitor.lib.mjs` | 1416 | 1156 | `session-monitor.queries.lib.mjs` |
| `src/claude.lib.mjs` | 1401 | 1247 | `claude.session-tokens.lib.mjs` |
| `src/solve.mjs` | 1398 | 1248 | `solve.mode.lib.mjs` |
| `src/telegram-solve-queue.lib.mjs` | 1374 | 1121 | `telegram-solve-queue.throttling.lib.mjs` |
| `src/codex.lib.mjs` | 1367 | 1250 | `codex.diagnostics.lib.mjs` |
| `src/solve.auto-pr.lib.mjs` | 1361 | 1225 | `solve.auto-pr-push-sync.lib.mjs` |
| `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs` | 1357 | 1084 | `isolation-runner.parsers.lib.mjs` |

`bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh` now reports no "approaching" files. One extraction also removed an accidental lint exemption: the auto-continue fork check now goes through `githubLib.ghPrView` instead of a direct `gh` call.

### 5. False positives

None found. The analysis records the two candidate classes examined and why each annotation was a true positive.

## How to reproduce the original failure

1. Add a ruleset on `main` with **Require a pull request before merging** and an empty bypass list.
2. Merge any pull request carrying a changeset.
3. The release job fails in "Version packages and commit to main" with the GH013 output above.

## Tests

- `tests/release-pull-request-2175.test.mjs` — classification of the verbatim GH013 output, run-scoped branch naming, merge retry while mergeability is unknown, and the end-to-end fallback from a rejected push.
- `tests/check-release-needed-2175.test.mjs` — all four release-gate states plus the exact output strings `if:` expressions compare against.
- `tests/hive-extracted-modules-2175.test.mjs` — behaviour of the extracted modules.
- Four source-level tests were updated to read the module that now holds the code they assert on (`test-issue-1829-compare-api-transient`, `test-issue-1716-private-repo-skip-fork`, `test-issue-1332-fork-name-from-pr-data`, `test-owner-fork-detection`).
- Seven test files now read module sources with `readFileSync` instead of `execSync(\`cat ...\`)`; all seven suites pass with the same assertion counts as before.
- `solve.mjs` was smoke-tested end to end with `--dry-run` against both an issue URL and a PR URL.

## CodeQL

The code-scanning gate on this pull request reported 14 new alerts (2 high, 12 medium). Both groups are fixed at the root rather than suppressed; the annotations are archived in `dev/log/issues/2175/pulls/2176/codeql/annotations.json` and analysed in `ANALYSIS.md`.

- **12 medium** — `Unnecessary use of 'cat' process` and `Shell command built from environment values`, raised against `execSync(\`cat ${srcDir}/<module>.mjs\`)` in the test suite. The pattern predates this PR, but the extractions rewrote those exact lines, so CodeQL saw them as new. Replaced with `readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` — CodeQL's own suggested fix — across all 55 occurrences in seven files, plus the one `grep -l` shell-out of the same shape that was only unflagged because its line happened to be untouched. `execSync` is now unused in those files and its import was dropped.
- **2 high** — `Incomplete URL substring sanitization` and `Incomplete string escaping or encoding` inside `dev/log/.../template-scripts/`. Those are verbatim copies of the upstream template scripts collected as evidence; this repository never executes them and cannot fix them. Added `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` with `paths-ignore: dev/log`, wired into both matrix legs, matching how the same directory is already excluded from Prettier and jscpd.

## Upstream reports

Both defects reproduce in the CI/CD template at its current `main`, so they were reported there with reproducers, workarounds and code-level fixes:

- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#143 — rebase-retry cannot land a push blocked by a `pull_request` ruleset.
- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#144 — release commits are unattributed (bot e-mail missing the `41898282+` prefix).

## Known gap, recorded not hidden

Seven test files fail on an unmodified checkout but are excluded from CI by the `@hive-mind-test-suite needs-triage` tag. Each was verified to fail identically on a stashed tree, so none is caused by this PR. They are a genuine CI blind spot and are listed in the analysis; triaging seven unrelated product failures belongs in their own issues rather than in a CI/CD remediation PR.

Fixes #2175

## Working session summary

The CodeQL failure is fixed and the PR is green and mergeable: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2176

## Root cause and fix

The failing check was the code-scanning gate, reporting *14 new alerts (2 high, 12 medium)* — the `CodeQL (javascript-typescript)` and `CodeQL (actions)` analysis jobs themselves were passing. Two distinct causes:

**12 medium — `execSync(\`cat ${srcDir}/<module>.mjs\`)` in tests** (`Unnecessary use of 'cat' process` + `Shell command built from environment values`). `srcDir` derives from `import.meta.url`, so an absolute path CodeQL can't prove is metacharacter-free was interpolated into a shell string. The pattern predates this PR, but the module extractions in `e0100587`/`be849c84` rewrote those exact lines, so CodeQL classified them as new.

Fixed at the root with `readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` — CodeQL's own suggested fix — applied across the whole codebase rather than only the flagged lines: **all 55 occurrences in seven test files**, plus the one `execSync(\`grep -l ...\`)` of the same shape in `test-fork-parent-validation.mjs` that was unflagged only because its line happened to be untouched. `execSync` became unused in all seven, so its import was dropped.

**2 high — inside the collected evidence** (`Incomplete URL substring sanitization`, `Incomplete string escaping or encoding` in `dev/log/.../template-scripts/`). Those are verbatim copies of upstream template scripts downloaded for this audit; this repo never executes them and the defects belong upstream. CodeQL had no path filter, so it extracted them as project source. Added `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` with `paths-ignore: dev/log`, wired into both matrix legs via `config-file:` — matching how the same directory is already excluded from Prettier (`.prettierignore`), jscpd (`.jscpd.json`) and ESLint.

## Verification

- **CodeQL: pass.** All 17 non-skipped checks pass on the pushed commit `838fd82e`.
- `npm test` locally: **all 412 test files passed**; the seven touched suites keep their exact prior assertion counts (14, 13, 19, 23, 16, 8, 10).
- `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check`: clean. Working tree clean, `origin/main` already merged, `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`.

I also archived the annotations to `dev/log/issues/2175/pulls/2176/codeql/annotations.json`, added the analysis section to `ANALYSIS.md`, updated the PR description with a CodeQL section, and corrected its stale "Three source-level tests" to four (`test-owner-fork-detection` was added in `73e678f1` but never reflected in the description). PR is now marked ready for review.

One thing worth flagging for your judgement, since it is outside what I changed: the PR still carries the recorded gap of seven test files that fail on an unmodified checkout and are excluded from CI by the `@hive-mind-test-suite needs-triage` tag. Each was verified to fail identically on a stashed tree, so none is caused by this work — but they remain a real CI blind spot that needs its own issues.
